app.name: Familee
app.title: Family tree
app.tagline: People, unions, events and photographs of one family
app.footer: Family archive. All data stays on your own server.

demo.title: Demo data
demo.hint: Creates the demo tree "demo" with the fictional Callahan family, so that anyone who runs Familee can see every feature. An existing demo tree is replaced and its people, photographs and files are deleted. Your own trees are not touched.
demo.warning: The demo tree "demo" is replaced with the fictional Callahan family. Everything in the current demo tree, including its people and photographs, is deleted. Your own trees are not touched. Continue?
demo.done: The demo tree is created. Open it from your trees.
demo.failed: The demo tree could not be created. The details are in the server log.
demo.slugInUse: A tree that is not the demo already has the address "demo". The demo tree is not created, because it would delete that tree; the tree is left as it is.

logo.invalid: Choose a PNG, JPEG or WebP picture
logo.tooLarge: The picture is too large (up to 5 MB)

delete.title: Delete the tree
delete.warning: Everything in this tree is deleted for good: {persons, plural, one {# person} other {# people}}, {photos, plural, one {# photograph} other {# photographs}} with their files, unions, events, places, sources, citations and notes. Members lose access. This cannot be undone.
delete.typeSlug: To confirm, type the tree's address: {slug}
delete.dialogMessage: The tree and all of its data and files will be deleted and cannot be restored.
delete.slugMismatch: The address does not match the tree.

tree.invalidSlug: The address may use lowercase latin letters, digits and hyphens, and must start with a letter or digit
tree.slugTaken: A tree with this address already exists
tree.slugReserved: This address is kept for the demo tree. Choose another one
tree.empty: This tree is still empty. Add the first person — everyone else can be linked to them.

fields.name: Name
fields.slugHint: Lowercase latin letters, digits and hyphens only

view.setAsFocus: Centre the tree on this person
view.hint: Drag to move, scroll or pinch to zoom, click a card to open the person. With the keyboard, Tab reaches the cards and the arrow keys move between them.

export.title: The tree as one picture
export.hint: The whole tree leaves the screen as one file: a picture to send to the family or paper through the printer, where the browser can save it as a PDF. The picture writes the names and the life years; the photographs stay in the app.
export.failed: The picture could not be saved. Try the SVG or the printer instead.

delete.title: Move this person to the trash?
delete.warning: The person disappears from the tree, and nothing is lost: names, events, citations, notes, the {photos, plural, one {# photograph} other {# photographs}} and the unions all stay. Bring them back from the trash whenever you like; only deleting them for good removes the files.

person.deleteWarning: The person will be deleted along with their events, names and links. Photographs stay in the archive.
person.dateHint: Write a full date as 12.04.1921 or 1921-04-12, a month as 04.1921, or just a year as 1921. In front of a date: “c. ” (about), “est. ” (estimated), “calc. ” (calculated), “before ” or “after ”. Ranges: “between 1915 and 1918”, “from 1915 to 1918” or “1915 – 1918”. A death date marks the person as deceased.
person.removeNameConfirm: The name is removed from the person. The primary name is not affected.
person.removeEventConfirm: The event is removed from the person, with its photographs' links.
person.notFound: This person is not in the tree

fields.headline: Short caption
fields.headlineHint: For example: “grandfather on mother's side” or “photographer from Tver”

family.childrenCount: {count, plural, =0 {no children} one {# child} other {# children}}

family.chooseChild: Choose a person as a child

media.hint: The main photograph is the one shown on the card in the tree. Click a file to open the original.

media.removeConfirm: Remove this photograph from the person? It stays in the archive if other people use it.

media.dateLabel: The day the photograph was taken

birthdays.title: Birthdays in the next two weeks
birthdays.none: No birthdays in the next two weeks

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.hint: Birthdays and wedding days of this tree, for the calendar app on a phone. Add the address below; it is the key to the feed, so keep it to yourself.
calendar.emptyMonth: No birthdays and no events this month
calendar.newAddressTitle: Give the calendar a new address?
calendar.newAddressConfirm: The current address stops working at once, for everyone who added it, including people who no longer have access. Members will need to add the new address to their calendars again.

trash.title: Trash
trash.hint: The people you moved out of the tree. Nothing is lost until you delete them for good: bring anyone back, or let them go with the photographs that belonged to nobody else.
trash.purgeWarning: {name} and everything that belonged only to them will be gone: names, events, citations, notes, and the photographs nobody else is linked to, with their files. This cannot be undone.
trash.notFound: That person is not in the trash

duplicates.title: Possible duplicates
duplicates.hint: People who carry the same name and the same years. The archive shows them but never merges them by itself: look at each group and keep the record that is right.
duplicates.empty: No two people look like the same person twice
duplicates.birthYearsUnknown: no year of birth in any of them
duplicates.confirmMessage: Everything of the other {count} moves to {name} - names, events, citations, notes, photographs and unions - and the other records disappear. There is no way back from here.
duplicates.merged: Merged: {names} names, {events} events, {photos} photographs and {unions} unions moved
duplicates.samePerson: A person cannot be merged with themselves
duplicates.notFound: That person is not in this tree
duplicates.placesTitle: Places that look like one place
duplicates.placesHint: The same name written twice. Merging moves the events, the photographs, the links and the notes onto the record you keep, and its children become children of that one.
duplicates.sourcesTitle: Sources that look like one source
duplicates.sourcesHint: The same title written twice. Merging moves the citations onto the record you keep.
duplicates.noPlaces: No two places look like the same place twice
duplicates.noSources: No two sources look like the same source twice
duplicates.confirmRecordMessage: Everything of the other {count} moves to {name}, and the other records disappear. There is no way back from here.
duplicates.mergedRecords: {count, plural, one {Merged # record} other {Merged # records}}; {moved} references moved
duplicates.uses: {count, plural, =0 {nothing points at it yet} one {# record points at it} other {# records point at it}}
duplicates.sameRecord: A record cannot be merged with itself

checks.title: Data check
checks.hint: Dates and relations that look impossible, gathered from the whole archive. Nothing is changed here - the records are linked, and the decision is yours.
checks.empty: Nothing doubtful found. The dates and the relations agree.

issues.implausibleAge: The person lived {age, plural, one {# year} other {# years}}.
issues.futureBirth: The birth date is in the future.
issues.futureDeath: The death date is in the future.
issues.marriageBeforeBirth: The marriage is recorded before a partner's birth.
issues.duplicateBirth: {count, plural, one {# birth event} other {# birth events}} on one person
issues.duplicateDeath: {count, plural, one {# death event} other {# death events}} on one person

gallery.looseHint: Files that are in nobody's album: taken off their last album, never attached, or attached only to the event of a union. An editor can delete a file that nothing uses.

steps.title: What to do next
steps.one: Create a tree and add the first person — yourself, for instance.
steps.two: Link parents, spouses and children: the cards arrange themselves into a tree.
steps.three: Upload photographs and record sources — certificates, registers, letters.

gedcom.importHint: A .ged file from another genealogy program (any version of GEDCOM)
gedcom.exportHint: A GEDCOM 7.0 file that opens in any genealogy program
gedcom.dryRun: Preview what would be added first
gedcom.empty: No people were found in the file
gedcom.alreadyImported: This file looks already imported: the tree already has people or unions with its identifiers (@I1@, @F1@…), so the import was stopped. A different file whose identifiers are the same cannot be added to this tree yet: import it into a new tree.

gedcom.joinSummary: New people: {created}; joined to people already in the tree: {joined}
gedcom.duplicates: People who are already in the tree
gedcom.duplicatesHint: {count, plural, one {# person of the file has the same surname, given name and year of birth as somebody in the tree, and no other patronymic: the import joins him to that record and adds only what it lacks.} other {# people of the file have the same surname, given name and year of birth as somebody in the tree, and no other patronymic: the import joins them to those records and adds only what they lack.}} Everybody else is added as a new person; the duplicates page can merge them later.
gedcom.doneJoined: {count, plural, one {# of them joined a record already in the tree} other {# of them joined records already in the tree}}

plan.repeatedChild: the child {person} is listed in the union more than once
plan.partnerIsChild: {person} is both a partner and a child of the union
